slide_title: How many filters we should apply

bullets: Visual features are common for different parts of one or multiple image
It is not required to use different filters for different spatial locations  in the image
(in other words, apply same filter for ALL positions in the image)
labels: Apply Red filter to detect ears in the whole image (not necessarily in the middle of the image)
Apply filter to detect nose in the whole image
Apply Green filter to detect edges in the whole image

layout.hierarchy: Title dominates (largest, bold, red). Hypothesis/Conclusion box text is next in size (serif, black, with the yellow-highlighted red phrase drawing the eye). Photos are mid-size visual anchors. Bottom annotation lines are smallest (italic, blue).

visual_elements.description: Large rectangle with thin blue border and white fill containing all hypothesis/conclusion text. Inside it, the phrase 'apply same filter for ALL positions in the image' has a solid yellow highlight behind bold red text.
visual_elements.position: upper-middle, spanning almost full slide width

visual_elements.description: Left photo: Grumpy Cat lying on a gray-blue blanket; white sans-serif caption with dark outline reads 'I LOVE MATH' (top) and 'IT MAKES PEOPLE CRY!' (bottom). Overlaid detection rectangles: two small red rectangles on the cat's ears (upper-left and upper-right of head), one yellow rectangle around the nose/muzzle center, two green rectangles on the left side near the blanket edge. A white mouse-cursor arrow is visible near the right edge of the photo. Thin red border frames the whole photo.

Right photo: small fluffy white-and-tan dog lying in a dark brown leather armchair/bed, warm indoor background. Overlaid detection rectangles: one red rectangle on the dog's ear/head, one yellow rectangle around the nose, two overlapping green rectangles on the right side near the chair edge. Thin red border frames the whole photo.

Bottom annotation box: light-yellow fill, thin blue border, three lines of italic blue text. Line 1: the word 'Red' is colored red. Line 2: after 'Apply' there is a blank space highlighted in solid yellow (representing the yellow filter). Line 3: the word 'Green' is colored green.
visual_elements.position: bottom strip, spanning almost full width

typography_notes: Title: large bold sans-serif (Arial-like), red, sentence case. Hypothesis/Conclusion box: serif (Times New Roman-like); 'Hypothesis' and 'Conclusion' are bold black headers on their own lines; body lines regular black. Highlighted phrase 'apply same filter for ALL positions in the image' is bold sans-serif red on yellow highlight, with ALL in capitals. Bottom annotation lines: small italic sans-serif, blue, with color-word accents ('Red' in red, 'Green' in green) and a yellow-highlighted blank. No numbered bullets; plain line breaks. No slide number or watermark visible.
animation_state: No mid-build state; all text boxes, both images, and the annotation box are fully revealed. A mouse cursor hovers over the right edge of the left image, indicating live narration/demonstration.
recreation_brief: 1. Set slide background to light gray (#E8E8E8); add a thin red (#C00000) horizontal line across the full top edge. 2. Center a bold red (#C00000) sans-serif title 'How many filters we should apply' at the top (~36-40pt). 3. Insert a white rectangle with a thin blue (#3333CC) border spanning ~6-94% width and ~16-55% height. Inside, in Times New Roman black: bold 'Hypothesis'; line 'Natural images are stationary'; line 'Visual features are common for different parts of one or multiple image'; blank line; bold 'Conclusion'; line 'It is not required to use different filters for different spatial locations  in the image'; line '(in other words, ' + highlighted run 'apply same filter for ALL positions in the image' (bold red #C00000 text on yellow #FFFF00 highlight) + ')'. 4. Place the Grumpy Cat meme photo (with captions 'I LOVE MATH' top and 'IT MAKES PEOPLE CRY!' bottom in white outlined caps) at lower-left (~18-45% width, ~57-84% height) with a thin red border; overlay two small red rectangles on the ears, one yellow rectangle on the nose, two green rectangles on the left edge. 5. Place the dog-in-leather-chair photo at lower-right (~48-76% width, same vertical band) with a thin red border; overlay one red rectangle on the ear, one yellow rectangle on the nose, two overlapping green rectangles on the right edge. 6. Add a bottom rectangle (~6-94% width, ~86-97% height) filled light yellow (#FFFFE1) with thin blue border; inside, three italic blue (#3333CC) sans-serif lines: 'Apply Red filter to detect ears in the whole image (not necessarily in the middle of the image)' with 'Red' in red; 'Apply ' + a yellow-highlighted blank + ' filter to detect nose in the whole image'; 'Apply Green filter to detect edges in the whole image' with 'Green' in green (#008000). 7. Optionally add a solid black strip across the very bottom edge to mimic the video frame.
